Rude and incompetent
Jan 2018 • Friends
I ordered a delivery from Cielo two weeks ago. They sent me a ham and cheese pizza without the ham on the pizza. When I phoned and asked them to send me a new one they sent their delivery driver round. He gave me a small plastic bag with 3 pieces of ham in it. When I called back the staff laughed over the phone and made a list of excuses. 
The actual food at Cielo is an insult to Italian cooking, The pizza dough is overcooked, the pasta lacks proper seasoning and the sauces lack the richness or flavour you would expect with Italian cuisine. Never order or go to this place they are a complete joke.

Wow, amazing... l am impressed, Italian foord raised to Masterchef level
Jul 2017 • Couples
Haha, now those of you who have read my previous posts will know l do not say "l am impressed" a lot, well. actually hardly ever... so a restaurant has to be good for me to lavish anything like praise on it lol... 

It is located on a main road and easy to find, the style is relaxed yet tasteful with a soft decor that is both pleasant, and easy on the eye. Such a design allows you to focus on your friends and your exquisite Italian food (and l mean to die for lol), rather than be continually distracted by blaring noise from cheap sound systems and the over the top mismatch of colours so typical of many restaurants in Vietnam. As always, less is more and this darling gem of an eatery is both delightful and relaxing.

The top chef and owner there (Italian of course) is Linh, she came from her kitchen to greet us personally and spent time with us to explore our tastes and preferences, listeng carefully and selcting dishes from the extensive and diverse menu for us. You don't get that level of service and quality in many places in Vietnam, only a small French restaurant in D1 in HCMC has teh same standard as LInh. 

I realise there is a pattern emerging here boys and girls, mmnnn, it seems that to be a top restaurant you have a be native Italian, French, Spanish or similar, (l haven't found an English one yet to share with you but will when l do), and also be the owner and chef to boot to make the grade.

Anyways l digress again, l apologise, l tend to do that, and this is Linhs review so l will focus lol... so, where was l?

After discussion, she offers a choice of dishes and when selection is finally made, Linh then goes to personally cook it from scratch. She also chose a bottle of Bulgarian (red) wine for us, (l have learnt over the years to trust the recommendations of such top quality chefs) and it was awesome, trust me... at this level they know their onions (excuse the unintended pun) haha, get it... they... oh never mind lol. We had a Basil salad with orange and lemon dressing with Prociutto, tomatoes, poatato and cucumber.

OMG, the taste was incredible the combination of flavour was exciting and moreish, and the tomato helped to clear the pallette for the next mouthful so it never became too much if that makes sense. Served with a garlic bread, it was a delicious and light entree to stimulate your taste buds.

The main course was Lamb, grilled to perfection, served with fresh roasted vegetables and a sauce made from apple and gogonzola, wah, that was incredible, and for desser we had a Tiaramisu but made with glucose so it wasn't overly sweet like the vast majority are. It still had the taste but was a delicious and refreshing change.

Linh is so good at cheffing, she is going to apply for Masterchef later in the year. For me, l wish her weell and l am sure she will go far.

ooh ooh, l nearly forgot, Ling will move a few steps along the stree soon and will have a brand new restaurant at 172 Xuan Dieu, Tay Ho, which she will creatively call 172... easy to remember and also rather chic and elegant l think.

The staff will also get a taxi for you so no worries there. All in all l have been twice now and always more pleased and impressed with ecery visit. You must try this for yourselves.
